common_name: Big Bubba Hosta (Unruly Blue-Green Giant Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; give it plenty of room to spread.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, allowing generous room for its eventual bulk. Big Bubba produces oversized, blue-green leaves with a loose, somewhat unruly habit, cupping, folding, and ruffling along their margins while picking up scattered puckering across the surface. The overall effect is a sprawling, good-natured mound rather than a tidy symmetric clump. Typical pale lavender hosta flowers appear on tall scapes above the foliage in summer, nearly lost against the scale of the leaves below.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Charlie Jane Hosta (Blue-Green Giant with White Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Charlie Jane forms classic rounded, blue-green leaves on a very large, symmetrical mound, keeping an evenly proportioned outline as the clump matures. Near-white flowers appear in proportion to the generous foliage, rising cleanly above the leaves in summer. Its balanced, uncomplicated form makes it a dependable anchor specimen rather than a novelty cultivar.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Combined Elegans Hosta (Large Ruffled Yellow Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; some morning sun helps hold the gold color without scorching.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade with some morning light to deepen the gold tone. This large, spreading yellow hosta from breeder Charlie Kwick carries tightly ruffled leaves with deeply impressed veins, giving the foliage strong texture and shadow. Leaf color shifts through several shades of gold and chartreuse as the season progresses rather than holding a single static tone. Lavender-toned flowers follow the typical hosta pattern, rising above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Dandy Lion Hosta (Sturdy Ruffled Yellow Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; tolerates some spring sun without leaf burn.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Dandy Lion is a sturdy, medium-to-large yellow hosta whose leaves carry soft ruffling along the edges and light puckering across the blade, giving the clump a cheerful, textured look. Its grower-tested tolerance to spring sun without burning makes it a dependable choice in warmer climates where many yellow hostas scorch early in the season. Typical pale lavender flowers rise on scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Emerald Chalice Hosta (Cupped Heart-Shaped Green Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Emerald Chalice, a Charlie Kwick introduction, bears nearly perfect heart-shaped green leaves that open into a wide, almost flat cup, catching light across their broad, prominent veins. The flattened habit shows off individual leaves rather than piling them into a dense mound, giving the large clump an elegant, open presence. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in summer, held well above the foliage.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Epic Blue Wave Hosta (Corrugated Wavy Blue Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Epic Blue Wave forms a medium-to-large mound of pointed, wavy blue leaves that fold slightly along the midrib and show attractive surface corrugation. The leaf margins undulate continuously rather than sitting flat, giving the clump a restless, rippling texture that holds up well as a nursery and garden plant. Pale lavender flowers appear on scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Frost Giant Hosta (Blue Leaf, Yellow-Margined Giant Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; allow ample room for a very large mature clump.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, giving this very large cultivar generous spacing to reach full size. Frost Giant produces an upright, stately clump of large, pointed blue leaves edged in bright yellow margins, creating strong two-tone contrast from a distance. The architectural, vertical habit sets it apart from sprawling blue giants, keeping foliage held upward rather than flopping outward. Typical pale lavender hosta flowers rise well above the foliage on tall scapes in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Gold Elation Hosta (Tall Spreading Yellow Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; resists spring leaf burn better than many yellow hostas.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade. Gold Elation, a yellow seedling selected from 'Elatior', develops into a very large, tall, spreading clump with foliage that resists the spring sunburn common among yellow-leaved hostas, even in warmer southern gardens. The height and reach of the mature clump make it a strong vertical presence at the back of a shaded bed rather than a low groundcover type. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Megan's Angel Hosta (Yellow-Margined Sport of Blue Angel)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this very large cultivar needs substantial room to spread.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, allowing room for a very large mature clump. Megan's Angel is a vigorous variegated sport of the classic giant 'Blue Angel', retaining the broad blue-green leaf base but adding bright yellow margins around each leaf. The sport grows with the same reliable vigor and scale as its parent, quickly forming an imposing specimen mound. Pale lavender to near-white flowers rise on tall scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: What's Mine Is Yours Hosta (Cupped Dark Blue Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Originally shared informally among hobbyists simply as 'Mine' before being formally named, this medium hosta combines beautifully cupped leaves with margins that carry a gentle, undulating wave, an unusual pairing of textures on one leaf. Its color ranks among the darkest blue hostas available, occasionally reading almost purple when viewed in deep shade. Typical pale lavender flowers rise above the foliage on scapes in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Crumb Cake Hosta (Shiny Round Gold Mini Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; well suited to containers and small borders.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this tiny cultivar is well suited to troughs and container plantings. Crumb Cake forms a small, round-leaved mini hosta with shiny, rich gold foliage that holds its glossy sheen through the growing season. The round leaf shape and compact scale give it a distinctly different look from narrower, pointed mini hostas. Small lavender flowers appear on short scapes in summer, in proportion to the diminutive clump.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Fruit Loop Hosta (White-Margined Cupped Mini Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; excellent in mixed containers or troughs.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this small cultivar performs especially well in containers and troughs. Fruit Loop carries cute, round leaves that are cupped and lightly puckered, edged with unusually bright, wide white margins for its small size. The leaves hold good substance for such a diminutive hosta, forming a tight, neat clump rather than a loose sprawl. Small white to pale lavender flowers appear on short scapes in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: One-trip Salad Bar Hosta (Yellow Sport with Dark Green Center)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. A sport of the small yellow 'Lemon Kiss', One-trip Salad Bar carries very rounded, cupped yellow leaves centered with a contrasting dark green patch, reminiscent of a small head of lettuce. The leaves curve upward at the edges, giving the whole clump a cheerful, upturned look. Small pale lavender flowers rise on short scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Tiny Gems Hosta (Heart-Shaped Blue Mini Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; ideal for rock gardens and containers.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where it thrives in rock gardens and small containers. Tiny Gems, a miniature from breeder Tony Avent, bears small, heart-shaped blue leaves that build into a perfectly neat, tight mound. Well-proportioned scapes carry light lavender flowers above the foliage in summer, scaled appropriately to the plant's diminutive size. Its clean habit and consistent form make it a standout among true miniature hostas.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List

common_name: Twinkle Little Star Hosta (Star-Folded Blue Mini Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Twinkle Little Star, a Don Dean selection, forms a flat, dense mini mound of very blue foliage, with each wavy leaf folding into a distinct star-shaped point at the tip. The repeated pointed leaf shapes across the tight clump give it a sparkling, faceted appearance unlike rounder mini hostas. Small lavender flowers appear on short scapes above the foliage in summer.
sources: Green Hill Farm (Bob Solberg) Spring 2026 Bare Root Hosta List
